definition: The set of techniques (RoPE scaling, efficient attention, careful data curricula, memory mechanisms) aimed at making models genuinely use hundreds of thousands of tokens, not just accept them.
details: The set of techniques (RoPE scaling, efficient attention, careful data curricula, memory mechanisms) aimed at making models genuinely use hundreds of thousands of tokens, not just accept them.

explainer.lead: Long-context modeling is the set of techniques aimed at making models genuinely use hundreds of thousands of tokens, not merely accept them. It matters because accepting a long window and effectively using it are different problems.

tiers.eli5: It is not enough to have a giant backpack; you need to organise it so you can actually find things inside.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply RoPE scaling, efficient attention, careful data curricula and memory mechanisms to stretch usable context. A pitfall is measuring only that a model accepts long inputs rather than testing whether it uses the content correctly.
tiers.paperLevel: The technique family includes RoPE scaling, efficient attention variants, data curricula and memory mechanisms; success is judged on effective use of long inputs, not just the nominal window size.

explainer.example: Extending positional scaling and training on progressively longer documents lets a model answer questions about material placed deep in a 200k-token input.
